newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-GRAND NATIONAL TO BE RUN ON MONDAY, POLICE SAY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-GRAND NATIONAL TO BE RUN ON MONDAY, POLICE SAY.

text.p: LIVERPOOL, England, April 6 - Britain's Grand National steeplechase, called off on Saturday because of a bomb scare, will be run on Monday, police said on Sunday.
The decision was taken after talks with trainers, owners and other interested parties.
Police sources said the race had been rescheduled for 1600 GMT on Monday.
A crowd of 70,000 were evacuated from the race course on Saturday after two coded bomb warnings. Three controlled explosions were carried out on packages later deemed to be harmless.

Thousands of people were prevented from returning to their cars as police and bomb disposal experts checked all vehicles at the course. Many racegoers spent the night in local sports halls and schools and were hoping to collect their cars on Sunday.
Four years ago the National was called off completely after two false starts. Half the horses completed the course and it was felt a rerun two days later would not be fair.
